Examination shows focal right lower-quadrant tenderness without generalized rigidity. A limited transabdominal study shows an empty uterine cavity, does not resolve the adnexa separately and does not visualize the appendix. No earlier scan has confirmed an intrauterine pregnancy.
after.Task: Which same-day diagnostic plan should be prioritized for {patientName}'s focal pain and bleeding despite the falling serum hCG?
Options: Appendiceal magnetic resonance imaging with general-surgical assessment
Diagnostic uterine aspiration with histopathologic assessment

accepted.explanation: Falling hCG does not locate a pregnancy or exclude an ectopic pregnancy. Persistent focal pain and spotting warrant same-day transvaginal ultrasound and gynecologic assessment. The specialist team must arrange follow-up if the location remains uncertain.

after.Presentation: {patientName}, a 49-year-old man with obesity, attends clinic before major abdominal surgery. His partner reports loud snoring and repeated pauses in breathing during sleep. Serum bicarbonate is raised on repeated measurements. He reports no vomiting, takes no diuretic and has no known chronic lung or neuromuscular disease. He is comfortable and alert at the visit.
after.Task: Which investigation should clarify the significance of {patientName}'s persistently raised serum bicarbonate before major surgery?

accepted.explanation: Obesity, sleep-disordered breathing and persistently raised bicarbonate raise concern for obesity hypoventilation syndrome. Obtain an awake arterial blood gas to measure carbon dioxide. Sleep testing remains part of the wider assessment. Bicarbonate alone does not confirm awake hypoventilation.

Coordinated fresh/fixed allocation retains both architecture and the opportunity for fresh-cell ancillary testing. An outside core biopsy showed atypical lymphoid cells but insufficient architecture for classification. The node remains superficial and mobile. Surgical review finds acceptable operative risk. The team can discuss specimen allocation with the receiving hematopathology service before the procedure.
after.Task: Which biopsy and specimen-handling plan should {patientName}'s team request next for suspected post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder?
Options: **KEY:** Excisional lymph-node biopsy with fresh flow-cytometry tissue plus fixed histology tissue
Image-guided core biopsy with fresh flow-cytometry tissue plus fixed histology tissue
Excisional lymph-node biopsy with whole-specimen formalin fixation for paraffin-based studies
Image-guided core biopsy with whole-specimen formalin fixation for paraffin-based studies

accepted.explanation: Coordinate the excisional biopsy and specimen allocation with the receiving hematopathology service. Send the specimen unfixed under its agreed transport protocol. The laboratory preserves a fresh portion for flow cytometry and fixes an adequate portion for histology. The accessible node and acceptable operative risk favor excision after inadequate core sampling. The laboratory must still assess viability and diagnostic adequacy.
